reference_solution.expected_approach: Use a stack to keep track of opening brackets and match each closing bracket with the most recently opened bracket.
reference_solution.why: The stack follows the last-in-first-out order required for properly nested brackets, allowing each closing bracket to be matched with the correct opening bracket.
detailed_explanation: Traverse the string from left to right.
For each opening bracket, push it onto the stack.
For each closing bracket, check whether the stack is empty or whether its top does not match the corresponding opening bracket.
If there is a mismatch, the string is invalid.
If the closing bracket matches the top of the stack, pop the opening bracket.
After traversing the entire string, the string is valid only if the stack is empty.
pseudocode: For each character in the string:
If the character is an opening bracket, push it onto the stack.
Otherwise, check whether the stack is non-empty and the top matches the closing bracket.
If it does not match, return false.
Otherwise, pop the matching opening bracket.
After processing all characters, return true only if the stack is empty.
reasoning_steps: Push opening brackets onto the stack.
For each closing bracket, check the top of the stack.
Return false if the brackets do not match.
Continue until the entire string is processed.
Check that the stack is empty at the end.

alternative_solutions.name: Repeated Pair Removal
alternative_solutions.description: Repeatedly remove adjacent valid bracket pairs such as (), [], and {}. If all brackets can be removed and the string becomes empty, the input is valid.
